description: Cross-language vectors for the typed job seam (include/tensorplate/core/job_request.hpp, job_result.hpp, job_event.hpp): frozen ceilings, stable names, validation reasons, construction vectors and per-job event traces. test/unit/job_value_objects_test.cpp replays every vector; every other implementation of these objects replays every vector whose scope is all. The notation block explains the shorthand.

notation.scope: all (the default): every implementation replays the vector. cpp: the vector needs an in-process buffer handle (a released buffer, a window offset) and only the C++ objects replay it.
notation.format: A PCM format object, or the name of an entry in formats. An encoding name not in names.audio_encoding stands for an encoding outside the enumeration.
notation.job_class: A name not in names.job_class stands for a class outside the enumeration.
notation.options: {language?, voice?, speed_milli?}; an absent field is empty or zero.
notation.pcm: {size, offset?, buffer_bytes?, released?}: a window of size bytes at offset (default 0) in a buffer of buffer_bytes (default offset + size, at least 1). released: true makes the buffer handle released. A transport without buffer handles carries size bytes of payload.
notation.text: {utf8: s} is s encoded as UTF-8; {hex: h} is the bytes h; {repeat: s, times: n[, then: t]} is s encoded as UTF-8, n times, followed by t.
notation.tokens: An array of token ids, or {count: n} for the ids 1..n.
notation.words: An array of word units, or {one_per_token: {text: t}}: word i covers token [i, i+1) and samples [512*i, 512*(i+1)).
notation.probabilities: Numbers, or the strings nan, inf and -inf.
notation.expect: accept, or {reject: reason}: error code config_invalid with the reason as context. For traces: accept (every step accepted and every job released), or {refused_at: i, reason: r}: steps before index i are accepted and step i is refused with error code inference_failed and context r, changing nothing.
notation.trace_steps: job names an entry of jobs. {job, cancel: true} records a successful cancellation (JobEventSequence::note_cancel_requested). Any other step is an event of that job, with the job's identity unless the step gives identity; progress needs progress_sequence and result, completed needs result, failed needs error {code, message[, context]}.
